land.text: the county, which 'reverted to the crown' with the death of Renard II in 1055; 'définitivement rattaché au domaine royal par Henri Ier en 1055'

successors.note: The Champagne block (Sens and Joigny) is held by county-of-champagne in the Cliopatria shapes of 1003-1055 and goes to the crown in county-of-champagne's own 1055 loss. The French page gives two accounts of the split: one chronicler has the county divided between the king and the archbishop, the other has the king inherit it all.

capitals.name: Sens
capitals.note: The Robert II page has Count Fromond II building a defence tower in Sens and Renard II fighting for the city; no page lists a capital or dates a move.

correction.text: the county of the Fromonides, 'les anciennes limites du pagus des Gaulois Sénons': the Yonne without the County of Auxerre

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Sens row; the land sits in its Kingdom of France shapes). The department of Yonne without Auxerre resolves to about 5,000 km2; it is the shape royal-domain-of-france gains in 1055. The French page puts the county on 'parts of the Yonne, Loiret, Seine-et-Marne and Aube' and says the Montereau side went to the count of Troyes, so the real county reached further north and west than this shape (Montereau, Gatinais borders); that is not drawn (confidence 2). No page gives an area.

correction.text: the county without the nine-cell block at Sens and Joigny that Cliopatria draws inside the County of Champagne from 1003 to 1055; Joigny's county was a vassal of the counts of Troyes

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The French page: 'Joigny's county was vassal to the counts of Troyes' and 'Montereau was ceded by Renard II to the count of Troyes', neither dated. The block is subtracted so the two dossiers (county-of-champagne gains it in 1003 with counterpart county-of-sens) do not draw the same cells; the Sens town itself lies in the block, so the remaining shape is the Yonne round Sens minus the Champagne cells. Confidence 1 on the extent.

region.text: the county of Sens under the Fromonides

ledger.note: 987: the county of Sens enters the map under its hereditary counts. The French page: 'le comté devint réellement héréditaire sous la dynastie des Fromonides' (10th century), 'Un premier comte de Sens est cité dès 695', Fromond I died in 948, Renard I held the office about fifty years; Renard II, who died in 1055, was Fromond II's son. No page gives a founding date; 987 is the year the neighbouring dossiers begin (royal-domain-of-france 987, county-of-champagne 990), a bridge and not a date.

region.text: the nine-cell block at Sens and Joigny

ledger.note: 1003: a block at Sens and Joigny goes to the Champagne shape. No page opened dates it: Cliopatria adds the cells to its County of Champagne shape in 1003. The French page says only that Joigny's county was a vassal of the counts of Troyes and that Renard II ceded Montereau to the count of Troyes (both undated).

region.text: the city of Sens, seized by Robert II on 22 April 1015

ledger.note: 22 April 1015: Robert II seizes Sens. 'Renard II was excommunicated and underwent the attack of the King, who seized Sens on 22 April 1015', after Archbishop Leotheric appealed to the king against Count Fromond II/Renard II.

region.text: the city of Sens, after the settlement with Renard II

ledger.note: 1015: Renard II keeps the county as the king's vassal. Robert II page: Renard's compromise was that he would rule as a vassal and 'the territory would revert to the Crown' on his death; the French page: the seizure of 1015 'rattache le comté au domaine royal' while Renard keeps the title until his death. The page dates no end of the fighting ('As soon as the fight against the County of Sens ended'); the year and month are bridged, not read (the month only keeps the ledger in order).

region.text: the County of Sens, annexed to the domain

ledger.note: 1055: Renard II dies and the county is annexed. Robert II page: 'Renard II died 40 years later (1055) and with his death, the County of Sens reverted to the crown'; Crown lands page '1055: annexation of the County of Sens'; French page: 'définitivement rattaché au domaine royal par Henri Ier en 1055' and, after 1055 the county was no longer a political or administrative entity and was run by royal prévôts (paraphrase). The region is the researcher's reading of the Yonne.

wars.name: Robert II's seizure of Sens

zones.text: the city of Sens, seized by Robert II on 22 April 1015

wars.outcome: The king seized Sens on 22 April 1015; Renard II kept the county as a vassal and it reverted to the crown at his death in 1055.
wars.note: Not a Wikipedia article title: it is the episode of the Burgundian succession war (Robert II's fifteen years of campaigns for Burgundy) that the Robert II page narrates. Renard II had allied himself with Odo II of Blois (undated on the page).

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the shape is the department of Yonne without Auxerre, and the French page's wider pagus of the Senones is not drawn.

notes: Written 2026-11-01 for batch g-eu-b (4 pages opened, 2 English titles failed; budget 2-5). New dossier: Cliopatria has no Sens row. THE STATE: the hereditary County of Sens under the Fromonides, drawn 987-1055 as the Yonne without Auxerre. PAGES THAT FAILED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Sens and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Count_of_Sens (url_not_found; the English Wikipedia has no article of that title, so wikipedia is null here); the French page fr:Comté de Sens was used instead. NOT SETTLED: (1) the start: no page dates the county as a state; 987 is a bridge (confidence 1) and the French page cites a first count in 695 and Maynard before 800; (2) the 1003 loss to Champagne rests only on Cliopatria's Champagne shape (county-of-champagne holds the same doubt); the French page makes Joigny a vassal of Troyes and has Renard II cede Montereau to Troyes, both undated; (3) the extent: the French page puts the county on parts of the Yonne, Loiret, Seine-et-Marne and Aube and says it bordered Auxerre (south), Troyes (east), Blois (west) and the Robertian lands (north), wider than the Yonne; the dossier keeps the shape royal-domain-of-france gains in 1055; (4) two chroniclers differ on 1055 (split between king and archbishop against the king inheriting all); the archbishopric of Sens is not drawn; (5) Fromond I (died 948), Renard I (about fifty years), Fromond II and Renard II (succeeded 1012, died 1055) are the counts the pages name, with no reign years but Renard II's, so no ruler strip; (6) the 1015 contest: the king's seizure is dated, its settlement is not (contest_end is a bridge); royal-domain-of-france has no 1015 event. (7) The county was in royal hands from 1015 on the French page's reading ('rattache le comté au domaine royal'); the dossier follows the Robert II page and royal-domain-of-france (1055). Gazetteer names needed: place Sens (the gazetteer lacks it), place Joigny.
